permit.applies: The employer applies: its covering letter of application goes with the completed Form 3.
permit.first: Proof the post was advertised (a full-page advert), police clearance from the country of origin, qualification certificates, a medical certificate and the employer's certificate of incorporation (Forms J and C).
permit.feesNote: The fee has been E300 since 1 March 2021 (the Ministry of Home Affairs' notice of revised fees, as Common Crawl captured it on 9 August 2026); no later notice was found.

note: Eswatini was a blocker for the country on 2026-11-01, as layer 3's was then (in SLATE, register R-1660): no published rule on what a foreign performer must hold was reached. Employer-of-record guides speak of a temporary residence permit for an employee on Form 3 at the Ministry of Home Affairs, without a primary source, so nothing was modelled on them. Layer 3 read the route on 2026-11-03 (papers.work.SZ, R-9719), in the Ministry of Home Affairs' Permits page as Common Crawl captured it: the temporary residence permit's Part I for employees, on Form 3 with the employer's covering letter, and its application fee of E300 since 1 March 2021. When this file was written on 2026-11-01 its permit's facts weren't sought again, so they stayed blocked until 2026-11-04, the route's source, read for layer 3, being the lead for the next search. Brought in on 2026-11-04 (HANDOFF's next step 3): the route layer 3 read (papers.work.SZ, R-9719), read again today in Common Crawl's captures of the Ministry of Home Affairs' Permits page (13 August 2026) and its fee notice, the live site resetting the connection. Nothing is said of performers as such, of the permit's term, the decision time or a short engagement; those stay unknown.
